decisions.question: MB-79 (p): a merge that brings a lane's round records is judged at commit time by R-MA's push-and-CI join (F-3 wording): R-MA note
decisions.recommendation: CARD-mb79-gapj-p (~/Buildo-scratch/p2close/CARD-mb79-gapj-p.answered.md), (p) option A, as worded by the MB-79 gates stage 3 adjudication F-3. Rule text: At commit time, during a merge in progress with exactly one merge head (`MERGE_HEAD` holds one sha), a record that the index adds against HEAD is joined by this row's push-and-CI source when the record is absent from HEAD's tree and its index blob equals its blob at `MERGE_HEAD`: the task is the `McBylaws-Task` trailer of the commit that adds the record in `MERGE_HEAD`'s history, and the prereg is read from that commit's first-parent tree. The record stays the round under judgement; every other loop check of the merge commit (binding against the merged index, oracle-first, add-only, record presence, the run) is unchanged. A record whose index blob differs from `MERGE_HEAD`'s, a record `MERGE_HEAD` lacks, a merge with more than one merge head, or a commit with no `MERGE_HEAD`, keeps the join by the prereg added by HEAD's commit. Conflict check: R-KW ("lane branches enter by merge, not rebase"), applied; R-LF and R-KU, unchanged (the merged tree is still bound); R-BG, this is the dated note it requires.

decisions.question: Card A, A-2: a Spec 69a row stops being owed when a dated status-cell note names a landed lock; the register generator reads it (build owed to a new MB-79 item, lane G)
decisions.recommendation: CARD-night-1101-four item 1: "A-2, the generator clears OWED when a dated note names a lock that has landed (R-KG "OWED clears by the generator"; M-246 "keeps the prior status text as its prefix"). Source: CARD-owed-clear-and-m409.md.". Card option text (~/Buildo-scratch/p2close/CARD-owed-clear-and-m409.md, Card A, A-2): - *The rule.*   - A status-cell note of one fixed form, for example `· *Dated note <date> (lane R; <source>):* LOCK LANDED <sha>: `<path>.test.ts``, makes `statusOf` return `owed: false`.   - Only the text **after** the last such note counts.   - It works only when the named lock file exists in the tree the generator reads. Otherwise the generator fails closed (the row stays OWED, and `--check` names it). - *What stays the same.* The prior text stays as the prefix, so M-246 and 69:7 hold unchanged. The same form serves Spec 131 rows, because the generator reads both registers. - *Compliance:*   - It applies R-KG literally ("OWED clears by the generator").   - It keeps 69:7 and M-246 (this is an M-246 note).   - It has no carve-out (R-KM).   - It needs its own lock (124:186): a both-directions `bylaw-register` test, red with the note missing or the lock absent, green with the lock present.   - M-60's note says this "would be a new generator mechanism", so it is a ruling plus a lane G build. That is R-BG's "changed by a §5 row".   - M-381 search: M-246, M-60's note, 69:7, R-LT (124a keeps its own form), M-382.   - The note must never contain `OWED ->` or `OWED:`, because `cite-parse.mjs:67-68` would read the row as OWED (lock-notes-plan section 2). - *Cost:* a generator change and its test, through the ten stages (lane G). It clears nothing until that work lands. Revised by the compliance proof ~/Buildo-scratch/mcbylaws/compliance/night-1101-four.md item 1, conditions 1a-1h, under the operator's second answer (q_n2). Rule text: In a Spec 69a row, a status-cell note of one fixed form, for example `` · *Dated note <date> (lane R; <source>):* LOCK LANDED <sha>: `<path>.test.ts` ``, appended in the M-246 form (dated, names its source, the prior status text kept as its prefix), makes the register generator (`scripts/analysis/bylaw/bylaw-register.mjs`, `statusOf`) read the row as not OWED. Only the text after the last such note counts. It works only when the named lock file exists in the tree the generator reads; otherwise the generator fails closed: the row stays OWED and `--check` names it. The clearing note never contains `OWED ->` or `OWED:` (arm C reads either as OWED). Scope: 69a rows only. Not covered: Spec 131 rows, and any 69a row whose last cell arm C reads as OWED by its own form (a leading `OWED`, `OWED:` or `OWED ->`; M-307 at this commit), which stay OWED for arm C until another ruling. Spec 124a rows keep their own form (R-LT). Nothing is cleared before the build lands; until then lock notes say "build owed" in lower case. The build (owed by this row, not done here): a new MB-79 item in lane G, through all ten stages with class G panels; the lock lands in the same commit as the generator change (124:186): a both-directions `bylaw-register` test, red when the note or the named lock file is absent, green when present, with the generator failing closed; the build adds no string literal beyond the R-LA baseline of `bylaw-register.mjs` (arm L passes, `mcbylaws/literal-allow.json` is not raised); the regenerated rule map, Spec 133, `docs/reference/bylaw-layer2-input.json` and the amendment index travel with that commit, and its table_version move is re-pinned under the operator re-pin practice.

decisions.question: MB-80 GAP-3: an out-of-bounds setting refuses the run before compute (follows R-G); amends M-428
decisions.recommendation: MB-80 GAP-3 card (~/Buildo-scratch/mcbylaws/MB-80/rule.md section 4; ~/Buildo-scratch/p2close/CARD-mb80-gaps.answered.md), option A. Rule text: Follow R-G (124a:121) in its own scope: "VALIDITY is per-variable via the closed `on_invalid` enum — `fail` MANDATORY for a verdict-/write-affecting variable". A declared setting with `on_invalid: "fail"` whose value is outside its bounds refuses the run before compute, as an unseeded setting does (SB-4). No row is calculated, so no row status is written. The refusal names the setting and the reason word `setting_out_of_bounds`. Today the executor's refusal names the setting with the reason `below_min` or `above_max` (config.js:92-93, :299-302); naming `setting_out_of_bounds` is owed to MB-31. Premise: `fya_placeholder_ring_min_n` is write-affecting, because it moves the written front setback, so `on_invalid: "fail"` is mandatory for it (124:68; R-G). M-428's reason word stays in the closed list, as the refusal's reason; its reading as a row status `not_evaluated:setting_out_of_bounds` is dropped. Worked-example form: "the run refuses to start and names <setting> with the reason setting_out_of_bounds; no row is calculated" (SB-3, SB-6, with <setting> = fya_placeholder_ring_min_n).
